[32310 Network Security Appliances | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This practical subject draws from the Network Security course provided by the Cisco Academy, with a focus on hands-on laboratory work centred around network security appliances. You'll delve into security technologies, products, and solutions, learning to design, install, configure, and maintain firewalls and secure routers. Key skills include implementing AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) and VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) using routers and firewalls. You'll also understand how encryption, hashes, and digital signatures collaborate to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.

[32310 Network Security Appliances | Learning and teaching activities]
This subject is a hands-on, career-oriented e-learning solution that emphasizes practical experience. It is a blended curriculum with both online and classroom learning.

 Students attend an internetworking lab class for 4 hours/week. It consists of a one-hour online lecture and three hours of combined tutorial and laboratory sessions in the lab.

 The lecture material is available online. Students are required to study this material in their own time before the class.

 Students work collaboratively throughout the Session. From week 1 students form groups and all lab work becomes a shared experience. All additional activities, such as researching concepts, exploring networking challenges and building the required networks are achieved by students working cooperatively together.

 Groups are also encouraged to share their findings with other groups, and whilst most assessments are individual, this shared knowledge contributes positively to the whole learning experience.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32310 Network Security Appliances | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Describe the theoretical aspects of computer security with an in-depth focus on modern network security threats. (B.1)
SLO2: Design, configure, test, manage, monitor and support network security infrastructure devices. (C.1)
SLO3: Apply network security theory into practice using industry based techniques, processes and standards. (D.1)
SLO4: Demonstrate practical skills on real-world commercial networking equipment. (D.1)

[32310 Network Security Appliances | Requisites]
Before you enrol in this subject, you must ensure you have met its requisites. The requisites for this subject can be viewed on its access conditions page.

Recommended studies
It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have an understanding of the principles and objectives of network security and of the fundamentals of network security technologies; CCNA-level networking concepts and skills, in particular CCNA-level routing and switching skills.
